About the Team
OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We believe that achieving our goal requires effective engagement with public policy stakeholders and the broader community impacted by AI. Accordingly, our Global Affairs team builds authentic, collaborative relationships with public officials and the broader AI policymaking community to inform and support our shared work in these domains. We ensure that insights from policymakers inform our work and – in collaboration with our colleagues and external stakeholders – seek to shape policy so that it aligns with and supports our mission.
About the Role
As AI agents move from answering questions to taking action across the internet, the standards that govern identity, delegated authority, discovery, communications, agentic-commerce and payment interfaces, agent-facing web access, agent-specific provenance, and auditability will determine whether agents can operate safely, interoperably, and with clear accountability. OpenAI is looking for an Agent Standards Manager to lead execution of our external technical standards strategy for a defined set of agent standards workstreams.
This role will work closely with Agent Security, Applied and Platform teams, Product, Legal, GRC, Global Affairs, and GTM to turn OpenAI’s technical architecture and controls into credible specifications, protocol profiles, assurance criteria, and implementation guidance—and to bring emerging external requirements back into product and security roadmaps before they become blockers. The positions developed here are technical standards positions, not broad public-policy positions.
This is a builder’s role as much as an external-facing role. You will execute a prioritized standards plan, author and negotiate protocols, build coalitions, secure the right internal approvals, and represent OpenAI in assigned technical forums. You will also help create repeatable processes that let the company shape agent standards without depending on a single person or relying on technical teams to carry external standards work on top of their core jobs.
The Agent Standards Manager is an integrator, not the owner of every underlying technical system. Security, Product, Engineering, and other designated technical teams retain ownership of architecture, threat models, controls, product decisions, approvals, and implementation. This role owns workstream planning, standards translation, drafting, negotiation, external representation within approved mandates, commitment traceability, and implementation handoff.
In this role, you will:
• Own a focused workstream plan for core agent identity, discovery, and delegated-authorization standards, with adjacent agentic-commerce, web-access, provenance, and auditability work assigned through portfolio prioritization.

• Recommend where OpenAI should lead, shape, monitor, oppose, or decline to participate within the assigned workstream, based on technical maturity, governance quality, strategic leverage, implementation readiness, and company priorities.

• Develop technical standards positions and normative contributions that preserve distinctions among the human or service principal, agent, workload or runtime, task, session, resource, and policy decision.

• Shape requirements for scoped delegation, attenuation, step-up approval, revocation, credential custody, runtime binding, discovery, interoperability, agent-specific provenance, and auditable action trails.

• Embed with Agent Security and Applied or Platform teams to translate internal architecture and controls into technically credible specifications, profiles, white papers, and assurance evidence without overstating maturity or deployment status.

• Lead review and approval paths across Product, Security, Engineering, Legal, GRC, Global Affairs, and GTM; maintain clear mandates, red lines, owners, dependencies, and external commitments.

• Represent OpenAI in priority venues and coalitions, such as IETF and OAuth-related work, FIDO, OIDF, W3C, AAIF, and relevant NIST or ISO efforts; build trust with peer companies, standards operators, and public-sector stakeholders.

• Bring external standards intelligence back into product, security, compliance, and go-to-market decisions early enough to shape roadmaps and avoid retrofit, launch, procurement, or market-access friction.

• Contribute reusable playbooks, decision records, contribution patterns, and handoffs that reduce key-person risk across the assigned workstream.

You might thrive in this role if you:
• Have strong experience in technical standards, internet protocols, identity and access, security architecture, applied cryptography, or closely related product or infrastructure work.

• Have authored, edited, or materially shaped normative specifications, profiles, drafts, or conformance requirements in serious technical standards or open-source governance settings.

• Can reason clearly about OAuth and OIDC, FIDO or WebAuth, workload identity, HTTP signatures, delegated authority, credential lifecycle, revocation, provenance, and auditability; you do not need to be expert in every layer.

• Understand that agent trust is a composed stack rather than a single credential, and can separate principal, agent, runtime, task, session, resource, and policy claims.

• Can distinguish adopted standards, stable extensions, active drafts, working-group proposals, and exploratory ideas—and know how that maturity should change OpenAI’s posture.

• Earn trust with engineers and security leaders while also communicating crisply with lawyers, product leaders, executives, policymakers, and external standards participants.

• Write clearly, negotiate constructively, and are comfortable representing OpenAI externally with discretion.

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's RL Data Platform team builds the systems that produce, move, and serve the human data Claude learns from: the interfaces humans use to give feedback, the pipelines that turn raw feedback into training signal, and the tooling researchers use to launch, monitor, and inspect data collection. Every RL run depends on a steady supply of high-quality data - human feedback, expert demonstrations, graded transcripts - and when a researcher has an idea for new data on Monday, our job is to make it collectable by Wednesday and in the training mix by Friday.

This is a full-stack, ownership-heavy role on a small, senior team. You'll design and ship web interfaces used by thousands of expert annotators, build the backend services and data pipelines behind them, and work directly with RL researchers to understand what data they need and why. You'll scope your own projects, make architectural calls, and see them through to production. We're looking for engineers who treat researchers as their users, build for reliability first, and care as much about the shape of the data leaving the system as the UI going into it.

Key responsibilities

•
Design, build, and operate the feedback and data collection interfaces used by human annotators, domain experts, and internal researchers.

•
Build and maintain the backend services, APIs, and pipelines that route model samples to humans and return structured feedback to training.

•
Own the reliability, latency, and usability of systems that run continuously against live model endpoints.

•
Partner with RL researchers to translate loosely specified data needs into well-scoped collection campaigns and the tooling to run them.

•
Build dashboards, monitoring, and inspection tools so researchers can see data quality and throughput without asking an engineer.

•
Identify and remove the bottlenecks between "we want this data" and "it's in the training mix".

Strong full-stack engineering skills, with production experience in TypeScript/React on the frontend and Python on the backend.

Experience designing and operating backend services and data pipelines that other teams depend on.

•

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

An overview of this role

As a Support Engineering Manager on our US Government support team, you’ll own the end-to-end delivery of world-class support for GitLab’s US Government customers. You’ll lead a tight-knit team of support engineers who troubleshoot complex environments and enterprise deployments, and you’ll evolve how we serve this highly regulated customer base so their experience not only meets but exceeds expectations. You’ll be responsible for hiring and developing excellent engineers, building and refining processes, and partnering closely with other Support Engineering Managers and product and engineering teams to ensure GitLab continues to meet the unique needs of government environments. You’ll also take part in our on-call rotation during working hours and join customer calls and ticket reviews when needed, giving you direct insight into customer challenges and the opportunity to shape how GitLab delivers secure, reliable support for critical government systems.

What you’ll do

• Lead a team of Support Engineers focused on troubleshooting complex environments for US Government customers and ensuring high-quality case resolution.

• Collaborate with other Support Engineering Managers to design, refine, and evolve our support model, processes, and tooling.

• Drive hiring efforts to build and grow a strong team, from sourcing and interviewing to onboarding and developing Support Engineers.

• Partner with product and engineering teams to share customer insights and influence how GitLab’s products and services evolve for government use cases.

• Participate in the manager on-call rotation during working hours to coordinate responses to escalated and critical customer situations.

• Support your team by joining customer calls, reviewing tickets, and providing hands-on guidance for complex or sensitive issues.

• Coach and mentor Support Engineers on technical troubleshooting, communication, and professional development, with a focus on customer-centered outcomes.

• Champion continuous improvement by identifying patterns in government customer needs and implementing changes that enhance our overall support experience.

What you’ll bring

• Experience leading and developing support engineering teams, including during periods of growth and change.

• Background managing technical support for complex enterprise products, ideally in environments with sensitive or regulated data.

• Familiarity with US Government customers and how their needs, processes, and constraints differ from private sector organizations.

• Ability to hire, onboard, and grow support engineers, with a focus on building balanced teams that can meet evolving customer needs.

• Skill in coaching and mentoring engineers through challenging customer issues, escalations, and professional development conversations.

• Experience handling crisis or high-severity incidents in production environments, including clear communication with internal teams and customers.

• Comfortable collaborating with cross-functional partners in engineering and product to advocate for customer needs and influence product direction.

• Openness to candidates with transferable leadership and support experience, even if their background is not exclusively in government-focused roles.

Our US Government Support team formed in 2019 and has grown alongside the adoption of GitLab within government agencies. We provide focused, high-quality technical support for US Government customers, helping them troubleshoot complex environments and use GitLab’s DevSecOps platform securely and effectively. We are distributed across the United States and balance synchronous and asynchronous collaboration to cover customer needs while working in a remote-first way. We are a mix of tenured and newer support engineers, and we are currently focused on scaling our processes, strengthening crisis management for sensitive systems, and deepening our partnerships with product and engineering teams to ensure GitLab continues to meet government-specific requirements.
